slides.title: Object-oriented basics
slides.body: Classes model state and behavior. Interfaces describe contracts. Composition keeps code flexible when requirements change.

slides.title: Collections and iteration
slides.body: Pick the collection around lookup, ordering, and duplicate needs. Explain tradeoffs before jumping into syntax.

slides.title: Exceptions and flow
slides.body: Use checked exceptions for recoverable cases and runtime exceptions for programming errors. Keep catch blocks useful.

topics.title: SQL Querying
topics.label: Course topic
topics.imageSurface: linear-gradient(135deg, color-mix(in srgb, var(--dashboard-section-interview-accent) 18%, var(--surface)), color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand-2) 12%, var(--surface)))

slides.title: Filter before grouping
slides.body: WHERE limits rows before aggregation. HAVING filters grouped results. That order explains many interview query bugs.

slides.title: Joins by intent
slides.body: Inner joins require matching rows. Left joins preserve the left side. Start from the table whose rows must survive.

slides.title: Indexes and selectivity
slides.body: A good index helps the database find fewer rows faster. Low-selectivity columns often need a different strategy.

topics.title: Vue Js
topics.label: Revision topic
topics.imageSurface: linear-gradient(135deg, color-mix(in srgb, var(--dashboard-section-cbt-accent) 18%, var(--surface)), color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 10%, var(--surface)))

slides.title: Start with constraints
slides.body: Clarify users, traffic, latency, storage, and failure expectations first. The architecture should answer those numbers.

slides.title: Separate reads and writes
slides.body: Different paths can scale differently. Caches, queues, replicas, and indexes each solve a specific pressure point.

slides.title: Name the tradeoff
slides.body: Every design buys something and spends something else. Call out cost, complexity, freshness, and operational risk.
